scope: Primary-source refresh on analytic forcing regularity, the unforced positive-defect target, and the announced explanatory companion to the OpenAI forced Navier-Stokes construction.

records.title: Regularity of asymptotically axisymmetric solutions to the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with analytic forcing
verified_scope: Suitable weak solution, smooth on compact subsets before the candidate time.
Force bounded in spatial C^2 up to the candidate time and spatially real analytic locally uniformly on compact time intervals before it.

Anisotropic derivative bounds on the angular mean through order two, and exact axisymmetry of the full velocity on a positive-radius ball at each pre-singular time; the radius has no assumed lower bound.
Under these hypotheses the candidate point is regular; application to the OpenAI construction uses properties stated in that manuscript and does not independently verify it.
records.reported_implication: For a solution with the construction's cited velocity properties and bounded C2 force, the force cannot be spatially analytic in the paper's local-uniform sense near the singular time.
limitations: Not a contradiction to a C-infinity smooth but nonanalytic compactly supported force.
Not a claim about molecular alignment, positional certainty, phase transition, or constitutive viscosity.
The authors explicitly do not independently verify the OpenAI construction.

records.title: The Positive Defect Problem: Target and Admissibility Criteria for a Programmatic Search for Unforced Navier-Stokes Blowup
verified_scope: Unforced, fixed-viscosity periodic Navier-Stokes problem, distinct from the smooth-forced OpenAI result.
Positive energy defect is sufficient for a negative answer to the addressed global-regularity alternative; converse is stated unknown.
The target is reduced to an averaged fine-shell energy-flux floor.
Paper states no finite computation witnesses the required Galerkin-uniform ceiling; its 128^3/256^3 spectral runs are exploratory for its own search.
limitations: Does not verify or falsify the forced OpenAI construction.
Finite-grid numerical observations do not establish an infinite-dimensional regularity or blow-up theorem.

records.title: Finite-Time Blowup for Navier-Stokes with Smooth Forcing, Part I: Construction of Self-Similar Solutions with Admissible Stress and Flat Remainder
verified_scope: Expository reconstruction of the profile-construction stage.
The record says oscillatory-pulse residual correction is deferred to companion Part II.
Bounded arXiv search did not locate the companion Part II at this check; this does not prove it is unavailable elsewhere.

repository_disposition: No issue or discussion filed: these are mathematical results and conditional literature constraints, not reproduced defects in the three solver targets or pinned OpenAI source repository. Existing solver gates and numerical verdicts unchanged.
simulation: None run for this analytic literature refresh.
